title: feat(machine): machine files name a default holder for new tools
body:
## What changed

**The key.** Two optional keys in a `.mch`'s `tooling` block (their own block, clear of #807's `spindle.rigid_tapping`):

```json
"tooling": { "number_of_tools": 10, "spindle_mount": "BT30", "default_holder": "BT30 ER20",
  "mount_source": "https://www.tormach.com/tormach_mills/ - MX machines have a BT30 spindle and tool holder" }
```

- `spindle_mount`: one of the holder library's tapers (`BT30`, `BT40`, `CAT40`, `TTS`). `TTS` is the holder system the R8 spindle on a Tormach PCNC or M mill takes.
- `default_holder`: a built-in holder-library entry, under the name the tool editor uses. Case and spacing are ignored and the name is stored in its canonical form.
- `mount_source`: free text the reader never reads. It records the public page the mount came from, because JSON has no comments.

**Validation, refused by name.** The rules live in a new module, `crates/post/src/machine/tooling.rs`, and three places apply them. The holder library is passed in by the caller: the post crate defines a plain `HolderInfo { name, taper }` and `HolderLookup` (`&dyn Fn(&str) -> Result<HolderInfo, String>`), and the app passes `machine::holder_lookup` (over `camcraft_tools::holder_library::find`) through its own `parse_mch` / `tooling_refusals` / `tooling_refusal` (`crates/app/src/machine/holders.rs`, shadowing the post crate's word-only ones):
- The reader (`parse_mch`) refuses with the first broken key, for example `machine file: tooling.default_holder: there is no holder 'BT30 ER99' in the holder library`.
- The Machines pane validator lists every broken key under its own name. The machine editor's "Tool changer and stations" group has two new text fields, Spindle mount and Default holder, that carry those refusals.
- `Machine::tooling_refusal` checks the machine stored in a project file (or a setup mount) against the same rules, and the refusal names the key (`machine definition tooling.default_holder: there is no holder ...`), not "a limit that cannot be meant".

It refuses an unknown mount, an unknown holder, a value that is not a word or is empty, a holder whose taper is not the stated mount, and a straight-shank chuck when a mount is stated. `LoadMachine::from_file` and `SetSetupMachine::from_file` now put the file path in front of the reader's refusal. Their doc comments already said the refusal names the file, but it did not. Nothing falls back silently.

**Behaviour.**
- New constructor: `AddTool::with_holder(world, name, tool, HolderPick::{MachineDefault | Named(entry) | Bare})`. The holder body is the same drawn spun profile `SetToolBody::library` lands; both now build it with one shared `library_body`. The body lands in the add's own `apply`, so one undo removes the tool and its holder, and redo brings both back.
- The GUI add path (`CommandKind::AddTool`) uses `MachineDefault`. The status line names the holder, for example "tool X added - holder BT30 ER20".
- MCP `add_tool` takes a new `"holder"` argument: a library name, or `"none"` for no holder body. A stated holder wins over the machine default. A stated holder that cannot be built refuses the add.
- `add_tool` now replies with `holder`, `holder_from` (`machine default` or `stated`) and `note`. `load_machine` now shows `spindle_mount` and `default_holder`.
- If the default holder cannot take the tool (a shank outside the collet range, or a lathe-held insert), the tool is added with no holder body, as it would be without the key. A note names the holder and the reason. No other holder is put in its place.
- Existing tools never change. Mounting a machine does not touch any tool. A project stores its parsed machine, so a project saved before this change has no default until its machine is mounted again.
- `AddTool::new`, used by tool-library import and tests, is unchanged and adds tools bare.
- **A machine-default holder never judges looser than the bare tool** (maintainer's rule, review-fix round). The drawn ER20 nut (35 mm) and TTS collar (38.1 mm) are narrower than the catalog's 44 mm x 35 mm stand-in cylinder just above the shank, so an assumed default is judged by the union of its bands and that cylinder (`HolderProfile::floored`, applied in `tool_body::judged`; the single-cylinder laws read its enclosing cylinder). A holder picked explicitly (`HolderPick::Named`, `SetToolBody`, the editor, MCP `holder`) is judged by its real shape. The document stores which: `ToolBody::machine_default`, set only by `AddTool`'s default door inside the add's undo step, saved as an additive `"machine_default": true` key on the tool body (absent = explicit, so every older file's holders count as picked; no version step), and a term in the operation stamp. The status line / MCP `note` says "holder X (machine default - judged no smaller than the tool's holder cylinder)".

**Machine files.** Source for both groups: https://www.tormach.com/tormach_mills/, quoted in each file's `mount_source`.
- `BT30` / `BT30 ER20`: tormach-770mx, -770mx-ml, -770mx-microarc4, -1100mx, -1500mx. The page says "the MX machines have a BT30 spindle and tool holder". The microarc4 file is not in the issue's list, but it is a 770MX with a 4th axis and has the same spindle.
- `TTS` / `TTS ER20`: tormach-770m, -770m-plus, -1100m, -1100m-plus, -pcnc440, -pcnc770, -pcnc770-s3, -pcnc1100-s1/-s2/-s3. The page says "the PCNC and M machines have an R8 collet in the spindle and use the TTS tool holders". Files that had no `tooling` block got one with only these keys; no tool-changer count was invented.

No new dependency between workspace crates: `camcraft-post` does not depend on `camcraft-tools` (maintainer's decision); the holder lookup is a parameter its caller in app passes. `Cargo.lock` is unchanged against main. The post crate's own word-only `parse_mch` (post binary, internal re-reads) keeps the holder as the stated word; it never lands a holder.

## What an older build does with the new key

It ignores both keys. The reader and the validator only read keys they know, so the `.mch` loads as it does today. A project saved by this build with such a machine has two extra fields in its machine object, and older builds skip unknown fields when reading. This is not a breaking change.

## How tested

Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/machine_default_holder.rs` (13 tests, all passing):
- `a_new_tool_on_the_770mx_starts_with_the_bt30_er20`: the BT30 ER20 lands with a 46 mm flange; one undo removes the tool and its holder; redo brings both back.
- `a_new_tool_on_the_770m_starts_with_the_tts_er20`: assumed, it is judged at 44 mm (floored); picked explicitly, at the 38.1 mm collar.
- `an_assumed_holder_stays_assumed_through_the_file`: the flag saves, reloads floored, an older file without it reads explicit, undo/redo keep it.
- `an_assumed_default_never_judges_looser_than_the_bare_tool`: the review's band (wall 20 mm off the axis, 55-65 mm above the tip) on the 770MX (BT30) and 770M (TTS): bare > 0 holder hits, default >= bare, explicit pick 0.
- `a_stored_default_that_no_longer_resolves_is_refused_by_key`
- `without_the_key_or_a_machine_the_tool_is_added_bare`: no machine, and `vmc.mch`.
- `a_stated_holder_wins_over_the_default`: a named holder, `none`, and an unknown named holder refused by name.
- `a_default_that_cannot_take_the_shank_is_left_off_by_name`
- `an_existing_tool_is_never_changed_by_a_machine`
- `an_existing_project_loads_unchanged`: a project saved without the keys loads and saves back byte-identical, and a new tool in it is added bare.
- `an_unknown_or_mismatched_holder_is_refused_by_file_and_key`: covers `LoadMachine::from_file` (file path and key in the message) and the pane validator.
- `the_shipped_tormach_mills_state_their_mount`: all 15 files.
- `the_default_holder_is_judged_by_the_reach_laws`: the reach pin. On a 770MX, a tool added bare misses a wall beside the flange height. The same tool with the machine-default BT30 ER20 records holder `FixtureHit`s. (The flange side only; the nut band is the test above.)

Post unit tests in `crates/post/src/machine/tooling_tests.rs` (with a stand-in lookup) cover the reader and refusals: absent or null keys, canonical names, unknown holders, holders off the stated mount, malformed words, re-judging stored values, and the word-only reader. Tools unit tests in `crates/tools/src/holder_profile_tests.rs`: `an_assumed_holder_convicts_the_band_above_the_shank_where_the_bare_tool_does` (BT30 ER20 and TTS ER20: the floored stack reaches the wall, the real one does not; never smaller than either anywhere; enclosing cylinder no smaller than the bare tool's) and `a_floor_with_no_cylinder_leaves_the_body_as_drawn`.

Review-fix round (head 7594010a, main 3bd54fc9 merged in): tools lib 56, post (all binaries) pass, sim `fixture_mesh` / `fixture_mesh_convict` / `fixture_mesh_posed` / `fixture_stack_span` pass, app `machine_default_holder` 13, `project_roundtrip` 71, `golden_cl` 25, `commands_undo` 32, `machine` 33, `machine_edit` 12, `machine_library` 11, `machine_assign` 3, `holder_library` 11, `tool_body` 12, `sim_tool_body` 7, `setup_mount` 6, `tormach_machines` 6, `mcp` 13, `mcp_setup` 6 pass; `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD crates/ui) 527 passed; clippy `-D warnings` on tools, sim, post, app, ui clean. No golden or snapshot changed.

Earlier gate:

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`. Because `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` changed, it falls back to the batch tier (all debug suites except the slow ones, the ui suites, and clippy `-D warnings`). Green on e15910b3: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app (1269 s, including `machine`, `machine_*`, `holder_library`, `tool_library`, `mcp*`, `tormach_*`, `project_roundtrip`), ui (CWD crates/ui), and clippy `-D warnings` on all eight crates. 0 failed, 44.9 min wall.

## Not exercised
- The GUI was not launched. The status-line wording and the two new editor fields are covered only through the shared code paths; no UI test names them.
- The camcraft-mcp skill doc (`.claude/skills/`, a process file) is not updated for the new `holder` argument. That needs a PROCESS_VERSION bump and is left for a follow-up.
- Machines that are not Tormach have no key.
- The batch tier was not re-run for the fix round (targeted suites above only).
- `get_job` does not name a tool's library holder. The tool body stores only `drawn profile` as its source; the holder name is reported at add time.

Changelog: Machine files can name a spindle mount and a default library holder (`tooling.spindle_mount`, `tooling.default_holder`, refused by name when unknown or mismatched). A new tool added in the GUI or MCP starts with that holder in the same undo step. The Tormach MX mills default to BT30 ER20 and the PCNC/M mills to TTS ER20.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #828
